research_question: How does the CURRENT production BIC lag-selection procedure behave in finite samples under platform-relevant VAR designs: how often does it recover the true lag, how does recovery depend on lag-2 signal strength, sample size, persistence, deterministic terms, dimension, innovation covariance and distribution, and are underselected models adequate lower-order approximations or inadequate models?
research_type: descriptive characterization; no method selection, no gate, no production decision

known_facts: In the v1.85/v1.86 primary grid, BIC underselects true VAR(2) designs in ~99.4-100% of replications.

Design-level (pre-simulation, deterministic) population algebra computed while building this design shows the v1.85 lag-2 template has psi 0.06-0.18 and that psi > ~0.29 is unattainable at persistence 0.5 with the v1.85 lag-2 direction.
known_information_disclosure.engineering_smoke_test: phase code 1, 3 cells x 10 replications; checked determinism and timing only; selection outcomes not inspected

primary_estimand: exact lag-recovery probability P(selected BIC lag = true lag) per cell
secondary_estimands: full selected-lag distribution (recovery matrix) per cell
distribution of BIC(1) - BIC(2) and of BIC(true lag) - min BIC
for true VAR(2): recovery as a function of lag-2 signal strength psi, never aggregated across psi
bootstrap diagnostic rejection conditional on correct / under / over selection (bootstrap_adequacy phase)
candidate_lag_set: identical to production: 1..min(12, floor((T-4)/(4K+1))), common sample, free parameters p*K^2 + K*deterministic_count (varEngine.selectLagOrder / maximumAllowedVarLag)

report_only_benchmarks.role: descriptive benchmarks computed on the same replications; no criterion-selection gate; no conclusion that another criterion should replace BIC

dgp.family: stable VAR(p) with deterministic terms; v1.85 templates, intercept, month effects and burn-in 300

designs.p2_v185: frozen v1.85 VAR(2) construction (weak lag-2 signal, psi 0.06-0.18)

signal_strength_dimension.definition: psi(T) = delta/(K^2 ln n/n), n = T - pmax(T); delta = population log-det one-step loss from dropping lag 2
signal_strength_dimension.construction: A1=a*T1, A2=b*T2 (v1.85 directions); b solves psi(132)=target, a solves spectral radius=rho
signal_strength_dimension.stationarity: every design has spectral radius exactly rho < 1
signal_strength_dimension.infeasible_policy: combinations whose psi target is unattainable at rho are recorded as infeasible with psi_max; never substituted or re-parameterised
signal_strength_dimension.purpose: map how lag-2 signal strength affects finite-sample recoverability; not to manufacture BIC success

bootstrap_adequacy.bootstrap: frozen v1.86 engine, recursive_iid_residual family (v1.86 selected), selection-aware (BIC rerun inside each bootstrap sample), B=199, h=12 adjusted Portmanteau, reject iff bootstrap p <= 0.05

categories.underselection_adequate_approximation: selected < true lag AND design-level approximate power of the nominal h=12 Portmanteau against the pseudo-true VAR(selected) residual autocorrelation <= 0.10
categories.underselection_inadequate_model: selected < true lag AND that power > 0.10

adequacy_decomposition.distinction: failure to recover the true lag (any underselection) is reported separately from whether the selected lower-order model is an adequate approximation or an inadequate model; the adequacy classification is a design-level population property, and the bootstrap diagnostic result is its sample counterpart

random_seed_namespace.reuse_policy: no spawn key reused; no alternative seeds; completed chunks never recomputed

monte_carlo_uncertainty_reporting: every proportion with its Monte Carlo standard error and Wilson 95% interval; BIC-difference quantiles with the underlying replication count; the uncertainty summary reports the maximum standard error per phase
decision_rule: none: v1.87 is descriptive. No gate, no criterion choice, no production decision. Allowed conclusions are descriptive statements about BIC recoverability versus signal strength, sample size and other design factors.
stopping_rule: run every preregistered feasible chunk in all three phases to completion; no early stopping; stop after summaries and the owner report; retain every checkpoint
prohibited_post_hoc_modifications: changing signal levels, reference T, construction or infeasibility handling
changing grids, replication counts, chunking or seeds
adding a criterion-selection gate or recommending a BIC replacement
changing production BIC, readiness, IRF availability or the production diagnostic
